review.source: Actual written N1904 and original Berean publisher rows, reviewed against displayed BSB; distinct peer pending.

6:1.sourceText: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ Πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
6:1.targetText: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.

groups.note: The English conditional repeats the same earlier action. The actual doing infinitive supplies the action in both positions.
Actual purpose construction with a passive seeing infinitive supplies the English infinitive.

studyHeads.note: Actual purpose preposition supplies the relation.
Actual passive infinitive supplies the seeing head.

groups.note: The actual otherwise formula introduces this condition. BSB phrases the condition in terms of doing the earlier prohibited action.

studyHeads.note: Actual conditional conjunction supplies the head.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening connective has no separate English rendering.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:2.sourceText: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
6:2.targetText: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

groups.note: Actual doing alms becomes this English giving expression. The actual almsgiving noun supplies the charity content.

studyHeads.note: Actual second-singular doing supplies the subject.
The actual doing predicate heads the idiom.
Actual alms noun supplies the charitable recipient expression.

groups.note: The actual trumpet-sounding verb supplies the auxiliary and activity under the distinct written negative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:3.sourceText: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
6:3.targetText: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

groups.note: Actual temporal genitive absolute and doing alms become the English when-clause.

studyHeads.note: Actual participial construction supplies the temporal relation.
Actual doing predicate heads the expression.
Actual alms noun supplies the charitable content.

groups.note: Actual third-person knowing command supplies the two English auxiliaries and its lexical verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:4.sourceText: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
6:4.targetText: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

groups.note: Actual appositional article introduces the characteristic seeing participle.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English spells out the object of seeing. Greek has seeing in secret without a separate doing predicate or object phrase.

6:5.sourceText: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
6:5.targetText: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

groups.note: Actual future be has directive force here. English uses a prohibition construction with separate not.
Actual purpose marker supplies the second to, introducing the seeing clause.
Actual third-plural appear/visible predicate supplies the English passive wording.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:6.sourceText: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ Πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
6:6.targetText: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

groups.note: The actual emphatic second-person pronoun supplies the overt subject of the praying clause.
Actual dative Father supplies the addressee relation.
Actual appositional article introduces the in-secret description.
Actual in-the-hidden-place construction is recast as English unseen.

studyHeads.note: The actual hidden adjective supplies the description.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual coordinator precedes shutting. English recasts the participial sequence as go, shut, and pray.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the local conjunct before the last imperative as part of its recast sequence.
English inserts a copula for the actual nominal location phrase.
English supplies the object of seeing. The actual phrase has no separate done predicate.

6:7.sourceText: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί· δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται.
6:7.targetText: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.

groups.note: Actual babbling prohibition supplies the auxiliary and lexical verb; the negative is separate.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:8.sourceText: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
6:8.targetText: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

groups.note: The actual passive likeness verb is a second-person plural aorist subjunctive in the prohibition with μή; it supplies English Do ... be like. The English command auxiliary belongs to this actual verbal predicate, while not retains the separate written negator.
The actual need noun and finite have verb form the Greek have-need idiom, rendered you need. Both source words carry the whole predicate; the have verb alone is not a lexical pronoun you.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek inferential therefore is not separately expressed in this BSB sentence.
Greek article has no separate English word in the possessive Father phrase or before the asking infinitive.

6:9.sourceText: οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· Ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου·
6:9.targetText: So then, this is how you should pray:  ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a cleft frame around the actual manner word how.

6:10.sourceText: ἐλθάτω ἡ βασιλεία σου· γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς·
6:10.targetText: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

groups.note: Actual written ἐλθάτω has the same third-person command role as the publisher’s Ἐλθέτω. Preserve the actual surface.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual connective expresses the heaven/earth correspondence without a separate English and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands the actual comparative elliptic phrase with an explicit subject and copula.

6:11.sourceText: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
6:11.targetText: Give us this day our daily bread.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:12.sourceText: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
6:12.targetText: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:13.sourceText: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
6:13.targetText: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

6:14.sourceText: Ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
6:14.targetText: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

groups.note: Actual future forgiving supplies the English future and lexical verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:15.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
6:15.targetText: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.

groups.note: Actual second-plural forgiveness supplies the implied subject and English verb of the first clause.
Actual future forgiveness supplies the auxiliary and lexical verb in the second clause.
Actual your trespasses is compressed to yours, retaining both written words.

studyHeads.note: Actual possessive of you supplies the initial study head; the noun remains part of the group.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB publisher Greek has explicit earlier trespasses and possessor after men. Actual N1904 has neither there. The later actual your trespasses belongs to yours.

6:16.sourceText: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί· ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
6:16.targetText: When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

groups.note: Actual plural becoming command supplies the English auxiliary and predicate.
Actual purpose marker introduces the showing clause.
Actual become-visible predicate is expressed by English show.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the opening connective unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:17.sourceText: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
6:17.targetText: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

groups.note: Actual fasting participle supplies the temporal relation and predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:18.sourceText: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ Πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
6:18.targetText: so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

groups.note: Actual becoming-visible recast uses an English auxiliary and predicate phrase.
Actual dative Father supplies the relation in the contrasting clause.
Actual in-the-hidden-place phrase supplies English unseen.

studyHeads.note: Actual hidden adjective supplies the meaning within the phrase.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The actual adversative sets the contrast; the translation supplies an explicit exclusive modifier.
English supplies the copula for the actual prepositional description.
English supplies the object of seeing, absent as a separate done predicate in the actual source.

6:19.sourceText: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
6:19.targetText: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

groups.note: Actual treasure-storing command supplies the English auxiliary and verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:20.sourceText: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
6:20.targetText: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.

groups.note: Two actual neither/nor connectives express the single English negation over moth and rust.

studyHeads.note: Actual second negative coordinator supplies the coordination.
Actual first coordinator supplies the negative scope together with its pair.

groups.note: Actual destroying verb supplies the first verbal auxiliary and lexical verb.
Actual not and nor supply one English negation over the coordinated thief actions.

studyHeads.note: Actual first local negator supplies the negative.
Actual nor supplies the coordinated second action under its negative scope.

groups.note: Actual break-in predicate supplies the second auxiliary and verb.

6:21.sourceText: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
6:21.targetText: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:22.sourceText: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
6:22.targetText: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the inferential connective implicit at the condition.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:23.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
6:23.targetText: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the final copula in the nominal exclamation; the earlier written is belongs to the conditional.

6:24.sourceText: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει· οὐ δύνασθε Θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
6:24.targetText: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.

groups.note: Actual second-plural ability and separate negative supply the fused negative ability clause.

studyHeads.note: Actual second-plural predicate supplies the subject.
Actual ability predicate heads the construction with separate negative.

unmappedSource.reason: English retains the alternatives after a colon without an overt explanatory marker.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an explicit two-part quantifier to the two coordinated objects.

6:25.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε ἢ τί πίητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
6:25.targetText: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

groups.note: Actual for-this construction supplies the inferential connector.
Actual worrying verb takes both Greek dative objects. English repeats the required complement preposition.
The two actual what objects share one English interrogative over eat or drink.

studyHeads.note: Actual first interrogative supplies the written head; the other remains in the same group.

groups.note: Actual comparative quantity is repeated in English for the coordinated body-and-clothing comparison.
Actual comparative genitive supplies the food standard of comparison.
Actual comparative genitive supplies the clothes standard of comparison.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:26.sourceText: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
6:26.targetText: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns—and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

groups.note: Actual third-plural sowing supplies its explicit English subject, auxiliary and lexical verb.
Actual comparative adverb supplies English comparative degree; the translation makes the degree more emphatic.
Actual distinguishing/surpassing predicate becomes the English comparative adjective clause, including its copula.

unmappedSource.reason: English introduces the observation with a colon and no separately translated introductory conjunction.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:27.sourceText: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
6:27.targetText: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

groups.note: Actual out-of preposition identifies the group of addressees from which the question selects.
Actual circumstantial worrying participle supplies the English means relation and action.
Actual cubit measure is retained as the source of the publisher’s temporal rendering hour; no hour noun is substituted in the source.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the introductory connective unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:28.sourceText: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
6:28.targetText: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

groups.note: Actual third-plural laboring supplies the explicit English subject and auxiliary as well as the verb.

6:29.sourceText: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
6:29.targetText: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:30.sourceText: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ Θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
6:30.targetText: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

groups.note: Actual being participle supplies the finite relative description.
English repeats the same actual subject as a pronoun under the elliptical second comparison.
The actual clothing predicate is repeated by English in the concluding rhetorical question, where the Greek leaves its repetition implicit.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a cleft frame for the actual manner adverb.

6:31.sourceText: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
6:31.targetText: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

groups.note: Actual worrying prohibition supplies the English auxiliary and verb, with its separate negator retained.

6:32.sourceText: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
6:32.targetText: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual emphatic all modifies these things. English repeats the referent simply as them.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:33.sourceText: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
6:33.targetText: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The BSB publisher’s Greek explicitly has of God after kingdom. The actual N1904 lacks that phrase; His remains attached to its own next-clause pronoun.

6:34.sourceText: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
6:34.targetText: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.

groups.note: Actual worrying prohibition supplies the English auxiliary and verb.
